summary: עָשָׂה names doing an act or making something, from everyday work to God’s making the heavens and earth. What is done supplies the particular force: keep a command, perform a rite, produce a crop, or deal with someone. מַעֲשֶׂה is the act or the work produced; the piel’s handling of the breast in Ezekiel is retained here, though its relation to making is unclear.

senses.definition: Perform an action or carry out what has been commanded or proposed.
Produce, form, or prepare a thing.

evidence.note: The craftsman made the gold lampstand.

senses.definition: Carry out a festival or offering according to its prescribed acts.

evidence.note: The resident alien wishes to perform פֶּסַח to Yahweh.
Israel is to perform פֶּסַח at its appointed time.

senses.definition: Act toward a person in the manner specified.

evidence.note: The servant asks for kindness toward Abraham.
God acted to preserve many people alive.

senses.definition: Of land or a plant, produce its crop.

evidence.note: Fruit trees make fruit according to their kinds.

senses.definition: An act is performed or a thing is made; context may say what ought or ought not to be done.

evidence.note: Abimelech speaks of deeds that should not be done.

senses.definition: The passive describes the speaker’s bodily formation in secret.

evidence.note: My frame was not hidden when I was made.

senses.definition: In Ezekiel’s image of two sisters, handle or press their breasts. These are the only two occurrences; the link to the ordinary verb “make” is not established.

evidence.note: עִשּׂוּ stands beside the squeezing of breasts.

evidence.locator: Gen.1.7, וַיַּעַשׂ → ἐποίησεν; Exo.20.11, עָשָׂה → ἐποίησεν

senses.definition: Something someone does, considered as an action.

evidence.note: The work the people are to do.
God brings every deed into judgment.

senses.definition: The thing produced or the workmanship seen in it.

evidence.note: The expanse tells the work of his hands.

doctrine.statement: Moses did as Yahweh commanded (Num 27:22), and Israel is instructed to learn the work they must do (Exo 18:20). The contrast is between receiving instruction and acting on it: James likewise calls for doing the word, and not hearing alone (Jas 1:22).

note: One verb holds the ordinary uses and Ezekiel’s piel; no etymological bridge is claimed. The spelling index assigns the same 2,628 tokens to p.fy.aa and p.fz.aa: only p.fy.aa is named so support counts are not doubled. The combined key therefore does not measure the piel separately. Proper names (including עֵשָׂו and the עשׂה names) and redirect-only keys are omitted. No scripture Syriac word of this root was found; עבד “do” is another root and is not added as though it were a spelling variant. The Ugaritic ʿšy lead has not been checked against a text and is not treated as established evidence; the Arabic sound-search matches in the brief do not establish cognacy. ποιέω and ἔργον are renderings, not Semitic loans.
